title: a no_receiver bounce leaves a line of the bus's wake state that outlives its scratch HOME
intention: Every no_receiver bounce the bus server makes appends one JSON line naming the bus's wake state at that instant (hook and _wired before and after the wake, the held shim's class, the bus pid and start time, the reason, the envelope), at a place that outlives the scratch HOME sweep.
why: Measured 2026-11-14: 69cd150dc116's two real reds ('codemother's shim could not take the envelope') left no record of the bus's state, because the scratch HOMEs that held their logs were swept; five reproduction shapes were green, and 69cd's D1 rests on a cause the code argues against. Its consumer is 69cd150dc116, which rewrites D1 from the first real line.
traces_to: Law 3 (nothing is known until measured) and Law 7 (errors permanent in records of truth).
how: In BusProcess.no_receiver (server.py) capture hook_before = to in bus._delivery_hooks and wired_before = to in self._wired, run hold_name as now, then capture hook_after, wired_after and the held shim's class (module.qualname, or None). Capture the bus's start time at BusProcess.__init__ (ISO wall clock, plus /proc/self/stat starttime where it exists). Append one line for both reasons. Inside a test run (CAIRN_TESTER_TEST_ID set) the line goes to log_path('tester', roots={'instance': account_home()/'.cairn'})/'runs'/<test>/'bus-bounces.jsonl', mirroring cairn/devices/tester/runs.py run_dir without importing the tester (RULE 1); otherwise to log_path('cairn', roots=same)/'machines'/'bus'/'0'/'bounces.jsonl'. account_home reads pwd, never HOME, so a scratch-HOME bus writes where the sweep does not reach. An OSError emits bounce_record_failed and never stops the bounce (Law 7). The proof provokes the bounce in a scratch_bus.launch world by posting to a name no shim answers, under a fixture test id, and trashes its fixture run dir after.

clauses.claim: a bounce in a scratch-HOME bus with test id T writes exactly one line at the account's tester run dir runs/T/bus-bounces.jsonl naming hook_before, hook_after, wired_before, wired_after, shim_class, bus_pid, bus_started, reason and the envelope id
the line still reads after the launch block exits and its scratch HOME is swept
with no test id the line lands in the account bus log, and a delivered ask writes no line
an unwritable destination still bounces the envelope to its sender and emits bounce_record_failed

decisions.text: D1: no_receiver records the wake state before and after hold_name and appends one line, at the account run dir in a test run and the account bus log otherwise; a write failure is loud and never stops the bounce.
D2: the red-first proof provokes a no-shim bounce in a scratch_bus.launch world, one tooth per clause.

out: cairn/devices/tester (its run dir is mirrored, never imported)

measured.saw: under bin/cairn test the proof read its line inside the run, yet nothing reached the live ~/.cairn/logs (no runs/testing-2a6a-*, no bounces.jsonl): the instance seal binds a throwaway copy of ~/.cairn (cairn/devices/tester/isolation.py instance_bind_flags), so a line written by a bus inside a sealed run outlives the scratch HOME but not the seal's swap. Both of 69cd150dc116's reds ran sealed (a pre-commit reseal, a verdict re-run). Carrying runs/<test>/bus-bounces.jsonl out of the swap before it is removed is the tester's, a sibling ticket (RULE 1), not this one's bounds
measured.how: find ~/.cairn/logs -name bounces.jsonl -newer server.py after a green --exec run returned nothing; read of isolation.py snapshot_instance_space / instance_bind_flags
